'''Olive Jean Dunn''' (1 September 1915 – 12 January 2008)<ref name="Basic Statistics 4th Ed" /><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.ancientfaces.com/person/olive-jean-dunn/84105648|title=Olive Jean Dunn|website=AncientFaces|access-date=2016-03-20}}</ref> was an American mathematician and statistician, and professor of [[biostatistics]] at the [[University of California Los Angeles]] (UCLA).<ref name="Author-notes-1959" /> She described methods for computing [[confidence intervals]]<ref name="CIs-1959" /> and also codified the [[Bonferroni correction]]'s application to confidence intervals.<ref name="Medians-1959">{{cite journal|date=1959|title=Estimation of the medians for dependent variables|journal=Annals of Mathematical Statistics|volume=30|issue=1|pages=192–197|last1=Dunn|first1=Olive Jean|doi=10.1214/aoms/1177706374|doi-access=free}}</ref><ref name="Multiple-comparisons-1961">{{cite journal|date=1961|title=Multiple comparisons among means|jstor=2282330|journal=Journal of the American Statistical Association|volume=56|issue=293|pages=52–64|last1=Dunn|first1=Olive Jean|doi=10.1080/01621459.1961.10482090|s2cid=122009246 }}</ref> She authored the textbook ''Basic Statistics: A Primer for the Biomedical Sciences'' in 1977.<ref name="Basic-stats-1st ed">{{cite book|title=Basic statistics: a primer for the biomedical sciences|date=1977|publisher=Wiley|isbn=978-0-471-22744-1|location=New York|last1=Dunn|first1=Olive Jean}}</ref>

== Education and career ==

Dunn studied mathematics at the [[University of California, Los Angeles|UCLA]], earning a BA in 1936 and an MA in 1951.<ref name="Author-notes-1959">{{cite journal|date=1959|title=Notes about authors|jstor=2282548|journal=Journal of the American Statistical Association|volume=54|issue=287|pages=695–698|doi=10.1080/01621459.1959.10501531}}</ref> She was awarded a PhD in mathematics in 1956 at UCLA, supervised by Paul G. Hoel.<ref name="News-Annals-1957">{{cite journal|date=1957|title=News and notices|jstor=2237182|journal=Annals of Mathematical Statistics|volume=28|issue=2|pages=533–545|doi=10.1214/aoms/1177706988|doi-access=free}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://phdtree.org//scholar/dunn-olive-jean/|archive-url=https://archive.today/20161117142843/http://phdtree.org//scholar/dunn-olive-jean/|archive-date=November 17, 2016|title=Olive Jean Dunn PhD|last=|first=|date=|website=}}</ref>

The title of Dunn's doctoral dissertation was ''Estimation problems for dependent regression''.<ref name="News-Annals-1957" />

In 1956, she was appointed assistant professor of statistics at [[Iowa State College]].<ref name="Ames Daily Tribune">{{cite news|title=19 appointed to, 21 resign from ISC faculty|date=2 August 1956|work=Ames Daily Tribune}}</ref> Dunn returned to UCLA in 1959 as assistant professor of biostatistics and assistant professor of preventive medicine and health, later becoming full professor and serving in that role until her retirement.<ref name="Basic Statistics 4th Ed" /><ref name="Author-notes-1959" /> Dunn served on the editorial boards of several journals.<ref name="Basic Statistics 4th Ed" />

==Contributions to statistical methods and textbooks==
Some of Dunn's 1958 and 1959 work led to the conjecture of the [[Gaussian correlation inequality]], which was only proved by German mathematician [[Thomas Royen]] in 2014 and was only widely recognized as proved in 2017.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.quantamagazine.org/20170328-statistician-proves-gaussian-correlation-inequality/ |title=A Long-Sought Proof, Found and Almost Lost |date=March 28, 2017 |first=Natalie |last=Wolchover |work=Quanta Magazine}}</ref>

Dunn's doctoral dissertation work formed the basis for her continuing development of methods for confidence intervals in biostatistics, and the development of a method for correcting for multiple testing.<ref name="Author-notes-1959" /> From the notes to her 1959 publication<ref name="CIs-1959">{{cite journal|last1=Dunn|first1=Olive Jean|title=Confidence intervals for the means of dependent, normally distributed variables|journal=Journal of the American Statistical Association|date=1959|volume=54|issue=287|pages=613–621|jstor=2282541|doi=10.1080/01621459.1959.10501524}}</ref> on confidence intervals:<blockquote>"Most of the research for this paper was part of my doctoral dissertation. The idea of writing an article for the research worker who uses statistical methods was suggested to me by one of the non-statisticians on my doctoral committee at the time of my final examination. In working on the various confidence intervals for ''k'' means, I thought of the Bonferroni inequality ones quite early, but since they were so simple I thought they couldn't possibly be of any use. I spent a long time trying to prove that the confidence intervals which would be used in the case of independent variables could also be used or dependent variables. After failing to find a general proof for this, I finally noticed that the simple Bonferroni intervals were nearly as short."</blockquote>The first edition of her textbook, ''Basic statistics: a primer for the biomedical sciences'', was published in 1964<ref name="Basic-stats-1st ed" /> Later editions were co-authored with another professor from UCLA, [[Virginia A. Clark]].<ref name="Basic Statistics 4th Ed" /> Dunn and Clark also co-authored ''Applied statistics: an analysis of variance and regression'', which has also had several editions, with [[Ruth Mickey]] joining the authors.<ref name="Applied-Stats-2004">{{cite book|last1=Clark|first1=Ruth M. Mickey, Olive Jean Dunn, Virginia A.|title=Applied statistics: analysis of variance and regression|date=2004|publisher=Wiley-Interscience|location=Hoboken, N.J.|isbn=978-0-471-37038-3|edition=3rd}}</ref>

== Honors ==

Dunn became a Fellow of the [[American Statistical Association]] in 1968.<ref name="ASA-fellows">{{cite web|title=ASA Fellows|url=http://www.amstat.org/awards/fellowslist.cfm|website=Amstat – American Statistical Association|publisher=American Statistical Association|access-date=20 March 2016|archive-date=16 June 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160616161612/https://www.amstat.org/awards/fellowslist.cfm}}</ref> She was also a fellow of the [[American Association for the Advancement of Science]] (AAAS) and the [[American Public Health Association]].<ref name="Basic Statistics 4th Ed" />

In October 1974, Dunn was honored as the annual UCLA annual Woman of Science, awarded to "an outstanding woman who has made significant contributions in the field of science".<ref name="Valley News">{{cite news|title=Luncheon adds up to politics|date=13 October 1974|work=Valley News|last1=Kabraker|first1=Audrey}}</ref> She was quoting as saying "I am thrilled to death for myself and for biostatistics...There are few medical centers in the country where a woman in biostatistics would be selected for this honor".<ref name="Valley News" />
